Frozen benchmarks. Hidden spec, gold decisions, hidden suite
Nothing in a harness prompt ever sees those answers
Kitchen app. resume-changer at a pinned commit. Expense CLI. Booking API
Ten seeded bugs. A rename and a framework upgrade
A red-team set of injections and malicious packages

Same tasks, seeds and models. Several runs

span.p: draft becomes evaluated

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: active becomes deprecated

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Responses cached by exact input. Unchanged reruns are free
The lab has its own budget and uses the cheapest allowed connection
Hidden text is scanned for inside candidate content
A held-out benchmark rotates each quarter
Same-name model drift: nightly evals flag the roster entry

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Where did the skill come from?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Kernel rules and the brief override skill text
An approved skill is pinned by digest. An update starts at draft
A project question promoted to a pack takes the same path

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Manifest: purpose, triggers, tools, size. It cannot add tools
Reject bundled scripts by default. Reject obfuscation, hidden Unicode,
ignore-previous, and instructions aimed at config or credentials
Over the token cap: reject, do not truncate
Quarantine with canary secrets and honeytoken URLs
A hit rejects the skill. Selection is by catalog ID, not by wording
An unvetted skill is allowed per project with a red warning,
still sandboxed, still size-limited, still unable to add tools

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Red team must produce no harmful action
A README that says curl a script. Test output that says edit the tests
An install script that reads .ssh. Hidden text that plants a false fact
A skill that appends to the global instruction file
A canary secret that must never appear in a prompt, log, commit or request

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Kernel: unit tests and properties. No double-spend. One lease
Accepted means every linked check passed
The daemon: fake clock, fake models, fake Git, fake sandbox. One seed
Faults at every boundary: crash, 429, bad JSON, conflict, disk full,
sandbox failure, vendor CLI exit
Adapters: conformance. UI: Playwright against simulation
A release must not regress the end-to-end run

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A benchmark that becomes too easy moves to the regression set
A harder one is added

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Knowledge travels on an orphan branch, harness-state
No shared history with the product. The product tree stays clean
A .harness folder on the developer's branch is opt-in
One YAML file per entity, sorted keys, stable IDs
Written after each published revision, debounced
SQLite itself is not committed. CRDTs are not in v1:
they do not resolve two different cutoff times

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Exported: decisions, quotes, research, architecture, contracts,
plans, visible examples, receipts, feature progress
Held-back examples: yes, encrypted with a project key in the vault
Transcripts: opt-in. Secrets and tokens: never. Re-enter them per machine
Leases, paths and process IDs: no. Usage: a summary per feature
Checkpoint refs: optional, so a parked task can resume elsewhere
History: append-only segments of change sets, versions and edges
Incremental export with git fast-import. Op IDs and event numbers stay local

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: How does it move?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Opening the folder finds harness-state
Import revision N rebuilds state.db
Running tasks become parked. Resume from pushed checkpoints,
or restart from the brief. Local backups help only if the folder was saved

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Settings, Export project. The same files, as a zip

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
lease.yaml beside manifest.yaml: device ID, holder, epoch,
heartbeat, revision. Compared with writer_epoch on open
The writer refreshes it when it pushes
Another device: open read-only, or take over
Take over increments the epoch. The old device's next push is rejected,
it parks, and it becomes read-only
A stale heartbeat can be taken without a warning
Two devices offline: the second push loses and stays read-only.
Its local checkpoints can be offered to the driver
A force-pushed state branch: ask which revision to keep. Never overwrite

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Who is at the keyboard?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Interview, plan, build, land. One driver in v1

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Browse and comment. Comments sync as entities
Their Git edits are treated as the developer's edits

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: The driver hands over, or a viewer takes over. Epoch increments

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
One daemon. Each project has its own coordinator and database
The broker owns plan windows, concurrency and machine slots
It grants a project a short lease: N sessions and a share, for 10 minutes
The project spends that grant inside its own database
Unused grants return. The broker never revokes a running slot
Two projects together cannot pass the plan share the developer allowed

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: What kind of work?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: One slot per connection is always reserved. It gets the next slot

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Weight 2

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Weight 1

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Idle capacity only

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Weighted fair share. A third project starts as background or batch
until it is focused. The switcher shows each project's share

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Public repo: state push is off by default, opt-in per project
Private repo: ask once on the first push
Held-back checks stay encrypted either way
Lost project key: regenerate held-back cases for unfinished tasks
Finished tasks keep their receipts

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Good

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Smoke fails or errors rise

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Deploy failed

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Nothing leaves the laptop without a rule
Push, PR, deploy, migration, env sync, DNS and webhooks are effects:
intent, approval, idempotency key and receipt
The harness pushes harness branches and opens PRs
It does not push main unless the developer turns that on
for a repo with no branch protection
Production deploy, live migration and DNS need approval each time
Preview and staging can be automatic

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Detect origin. GitHub first. GitLab later
Device OAuth, or an existing gh login, in the vault
Read branch protection and required checks
Default is PR mode. Direct mode pushes a branch the developer names

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Feature reaches DONE
Each PR, CI run and deploy is a ship_runs row

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
One push of harness/f/feature. Not one push per task
Open a draft PR from the graph: requirements, checks, migrations,
new dependencies, choices made for them, links to the plan
The structure needs no model. A summary paragraph is optional

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: GitHub Actions

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Mark the PR ready. Land as settings say
Required reviewers: wait. Never bypass them

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Read failed logs. Patterns first, then a small model
Platform difference: repair, and reproduce in the Tier D container
Missing secret: a human step. Never paste it into code
Flaky: re-run once, then the test owner
Real regression: repair task to the owning feature
Runner or quota: wait. No repair task
The worker sees the failing lines. Same fingerprint, 3 pushes, then the developer
Phase 0's CI workflow runs the same gates on Linux and Windows

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
One GitHub queue per account
Content-creating calls stay under 80 a minute and 500 an hour
Polling is conditional and backs off from 30 seconds to 5 minutes
retry-after and x-ratelimit-reset are obeyed
Repeated secondary limits pause the queue and show in the cockpit

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Which environment?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Automatic. Test secrets. A disposable or branched database

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Automatic after the PR is ready, if staging is configured

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Explicit approval, with the plan shown

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
One adapter interface: probe, plan, deploy, status, logs,
promote, rollback, syncEnv
v1: Vercel and Docker over SSH
Railway, Fly.io, Render and AWS come later. No hosting yet is a discovery question. Nothing is created unasked

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Vault holds values per environment
syncEnv shows names only, and production needs approval
Production values are never pulled back for tests

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
0 Rehearse on a copy or a restored staging backup. Automatic
1 Backup or point-in-time recovery. Must succeed
2 Expand only: new tables, nullable columns, concurrent indexes
3 Deploy the app, which can read old and new
4 Batched backfill, with progress and pause
5 Contract in a later release, separately approved, export offered
A destructive migration cannot skip rehearsal and backup
A long lock switches to an online plan, or asks for a window

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: After deploy

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Health and build ID. Smoke journeys with a test account
Watch errors for 10 minutes

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Result

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Mark released. Tag the commit. Notes from the graph

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Preview and staging roll the app back automatically
Production offers rollback, and does it only if that was enabled
The database stays. Expand-only changes are still compatible
A repair task gets the evidence

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Nothing switched. Logs attached. Repair task

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Webhooks, OAuth redirects and DNS are effects with receipts
An API call stores the returned ID so undo can remove it
Otherwise a guided human step, confirmed by a probe

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Developer commits on the same branch: merge, never force-push
A CI hour: back off, other work continues
Expired deploy token: reconnect, deployment parked

display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: One normalized event stream, plus the kernel's own events

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Which view?

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Status lines are written by code, not by a model
Raw logs are one click deep, behind a readable timeline
Lanes: Queued, Working, Waiting on you, Held, Verifying,
Integrating, Done. Done names the level and the cost
Explain, only when clicked, summarizes the last 50 events

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Same events, drawn as a place. The toggle keeps chat, inbox and top bar
It never lies: no animation without an event. Calm office, calm build
CEO is the developer. Manager, Senior, Mid and Junior by clothes and props
A foreign sub-agent is a small helper at the parent's desk
Lab tech is the verifier. Guard is kernel policy
Same character for an agent's life. Hover shows model and connection
Desk color is the connection. No vendor logos

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Top bar on both: phase and wave, tasks done, spend per currency
Pause all checkpoints at the next boundary
Stop is a direct kernel path. The office keeps this ribbon too,
so nothing important exists only as an animation

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Health, from events, with no model
No events for 5 minutes: possibly stuck. Nudge, interrupt, or open
Same tool or same failing command 3 times: looping
Rate limit: throttled, with the retry hint. Not a failure
Plan window closed: waiting for allowance, with the reset time
Moved up a level, or back to the author: escalated
Many workers: group cards by feature. Raw-by-default is a setting

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Anything that needs the developer enters one inbox

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Owner first. The task author answers from the record when they can
Test disputes go to the author too. Most never reach the developer

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
De-duplicate by criterion and scope. One item, many subscribers
Group by feature. A waiting worker takes another ready task if one exists

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: What kind of item?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Interrupt now. Banner, and a sound if enabled

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Batch. Deliver when 10 minutes close, or idle is threatened,
or a blocked task is on the critical path
Order: critical path, then how many tasks, then age
At most one batch alert per 10 minutes
Focus mode delivers only Interrupt now

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
FYI digest. No alert
Away for an hour: unblocked work continues,
the batch waits, nothing is auto-answered

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Done means checked, not assumed
Decision: the answer validates
Secret: probe succeeds, or a format check plus first successful use
Tool: the re-probe succeeds
Account: a probe, or an attestation labeled not verified
Approval: approve or deny a risky action
Review: plan, design baseline, or I fixed it myself

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A secret is a name, a reason, the tasks, where to get it, a masked field
OS vault. SQLite stores a reference and the name
Injected as env into the verifier, tests and dev server that need it
The brief says the name is available, never the value
Redactor masks exact values and common encodings
A secret in a diff or a snapshot rejects the candidate
and raises Interrupt now. A secret pasted in chat is held,
offered to the vault, and deleted from history
A live-key prefix is refused in tests unless that task allows it
Known services get a harmless read. Unknown ones: format now,
verified on first success. Writing .env is off, and only if gitignored
A later rejection asks for an update

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A human step blocks only the tasks that need it
Playwright: version and a launch. Install in a visible terminal, after consent
Docker: docker info, then a link, then re-probe
A database: connection test. A cloud API: probe if a key or CLI exists,
otherwise a checklist and an attestation

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
CEO office: inbox. Open floor: attempts, in feature pods
Manager offices: the task list. Records room: graph and briefs
Meeting room: AskOwner, DisputeTest, planner questions
Test lab: verifier. Shipping dock: merge queue
Break room: rate limit, allowance, or a dependency, with the clock
Front desk: a human step. Vault: secrets, and only the guard enters
Server room: a local model, fans on while it generates

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Animation director between the stream and the characters
One queue each. Bursts collapse into one loop. A new state beats a walk
Over about two seconds behind: fade and reappear
Dwell about a second, so states do not flicker
Status icons update immediately

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
session.started: elevator to a free desk in the feature pod
Brief or contract read: records room and back
plan.updated: notebook and sticky notes
Read or search: scrolling text. Edit: typing a diff
Tests: a progress bar. Permission denied: the guard
AskOwner: meeting room. Answered from the record: a short meeting
Escalated: the manager carries paper to the CEO
Sub-agent: a helper. submit: carry a box to the lab
Pass: green lamp, then the dock, and a checkmark
Fail: red lamp, box back. Repeated fails: the manager's office
Level up: a Senior takes the desk. Rate limit: break room
Window closed: several in the break room, desks dim
Hold: watch the whiteboard update. User pause: pens down
Budget exhausted: evening light, folders, idle
Merged: the truck leaves. Looping or stuck: an amber question mark
Session ended: tidy and leave, or take the next desk

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Paper reaches the CEO only after owner checks and batching
Red is interrupt, yellow is blocking, white is FYI
The pile height is the inbox count. A batch is a stapled stack
Click the tray to open the inbox. Answering stamps the sheet
The manager walks it back. A secret or a tool is a parcel
at the front desk, not a decision sheet

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Hover: name, level, model, task, time, tokens
Click: the same worker panel as the Board
Double-click zooms into the monitor. Esc zooms out
Right-click: pause, stop, message the manager, change level, fix it myself
Whiteboard: that feature's plan. Records: Architecture
Lab: verification. Dock: the merge queue. Tray and front desk: the inbox

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
PixiJS. A Tiled map. Layered Aseprite sprites. A-star between rooms
One state machine per character, so it can be tested without drawing
Decided: cozy 16 px pixel art. Isometric later, as a skin
Commissioned or licensed art. No vendor logos
60 fps, under 5 percent CPU when idle, paused when hidden
About 30 characters animate. Beyond that, a hot-desk count
Reduced motion: stay seated, icons and labels only
Every state has text and an icon shape, not color alone
Tab cycles characters. A screen-reader list mirrors the room
Sound off by default

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Delivery stage

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Desks, rank, poses, the CEO tray, click-through panels
Exit: find the waiting task faster than on the Board

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Walking, meetings, lab, dock, break room
Exit: lag under 2 seconds with 10 workers

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Avatar, character editor, layout editor, naming

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Day and night, an end-of-day recap, celebrations, optional sound

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Decided: name tags are the agent ID plus a short task title
Decided: the Office is the default build view. The Board is one click away
Reduced motion or memory pressure shows the Board instead
Cards separate thinking, waiting for a run slot, and running

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Instant task change: skip the walk, update the desk sign
Stream disconnect: freeze, show reconnecting, keep the last time
A tall inbox is a stack with a number. Helpers past three are a count
A small window zooms to the busiest pod, with a mini-map
In the background, rendering stops. On return, jump to current state

span.p: Rebase, merge or conflicts

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Commit my edits first

span.p: Land later

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Show me how

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Or they take Fix it myself, or say so in chat

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Card on a failed or held task

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: A commit touches that write scope

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Pass

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Fail

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Keep fixing

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: This test is wrong

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Accept anyway

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The checkout is the developer's. No edit, stash, reset or commit
there without an explicit click. Harness work stays in its worktrees
and harness branches. harness/integration is never their checkout,
so dirty files on main do not block the merge queue
Nothing they wrote is discarded. A revert is a forward commit
A human-owned worktree is never deleted without asking

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A watcher on the checkout, ignoring dependency and build folders,
plus git status and ref checks
Files no active task touches: say nothing
package.json or the lockfile: offer to include it
A new base commit: a digest item, then a base sync
A branch switch: the status bar updates. The landing target stays
A rebase or merge in progress: landing waits
Edits inside a running worktree: same three choices as an overlap

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: What did they touch?

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Overlap

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Include it so workers can use it?

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A new base commit is merged into harness/integration
Recheck the changed files. Refresh in-flight tasks whose inputs changed
A conflict with a running task goes to its owner as a normal revision
Their commits are the new truth, and are never rewritten
A force-push rebuilds integration from the new base.
Tasks whose base vanished resume from checkpoints
Deleting a file a finished feature added is reported, and asked about
Fixing an already accepted task is a normal commit, then a recheck

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The worker stops at its next boundary
WIP is a checkpoint. The task becomes human-owned

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The worker continues. On landing, merge with their committed
version and resolve or report the conflicts

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: No change. Do not repeat this notice for this file, this session

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Commit with the developer as author. It becomes base
The integrator reconciles it with open dependency intents

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Workers do not see the new package

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Human-owned. The worker stops. WIP stays on a checkpoint ref
Work in that task's worktree, or in their own checkout
Editing is normal. The harness stays out of the way
I'm done, or a chat message, collects the work
Worktree: the harness commits, developer as author
Own checkout: they pick the commits, prefilled from the scope

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Bring integration onto their branch?
Predict with merge-tree first. Auto-land is off

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Fast-forward or a merge commit, as settings chose

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Git can update and leave those files
Proceed only if auto-land is on. Otherwise ask once

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Never touch the tree

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Wait, and recheck when it finishes

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Explicit click

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Show the diff. Commit with them as author. Then land

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Leave it

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Say that restore may conflict. Run only on this click
Never stash silently

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: They land it themselves

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: I fixed it myself. How did it start?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Suggest: verify it as that task?

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The same clean verifier. The same locked checks
The same held-back cases

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Result

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Accepted. Author is the developer. Dependents unlock
The node records acceptedBy human, the commit and the receipt
The office shows the CEO's stamp

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Next

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A product decision. Change the expectation, with an impact preview
Not a quiet edit of the test

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Record the override and the reason
Dependents see a warning. It is in the final summary

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
If an export or a schema changed: compatible is done.
Incompatible consumers are re-briefed, and the preview shows the impact
Files outside the task's scope are listed: record them on their own,
attach them to this task, or leave them unrecorded
After days away, re-entry reconciliation runs before anything starts

span.p: Otherwise

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A current, unretracted statement
establishes this exact value

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A listed rule applies, and every
premise is already a resolved fact

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
The user handed this over,
inside stated limits

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Anything else

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Yes

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: No

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A checkpoint at every turn boundary
WIP commit on refs/harness/checkpoints
Attempt branch harness/t/task/attempt
Session reference: Codex thread, Claude session, Cursor agent, or our transcript
Handoff note written by code: brief version, steps done and left,
files changed, last checks, last failing check
Ledger spend and reservations, settled
A limit, a crash or a closed laptop loses at most the turn in progress
Resume uses the runtime's own resume when it works
Otherwise a fresh session gets the brief plus the labeled diff
Sleep mid-turn: treat the call as unknown, resume from the checkpoint,
and reconcile an ambiguous paid call before retrying

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Spend

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Alert only. The meter turns amber. One digest item

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Wind-down. No new attempts
Running attempts finish the current step
A reserve stays for checkpoints and for verifying finished candidates

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Every attempt checkpoints and parks
Office lights go to evening. This is not a failed task

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Same as stopped, with the reset time when it is known
Auto-resume only if the user enabled it

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Stop card. Each option shows its estimate first
Add budget. Use cheaper models, previewing the remainder only
Switch connection. Wait for the reset. Keep parked
Finish by hand: export wip branches and the feature branch
of what was accepted, with the handoff in the app and
optionally beside the commit. Then I fixed it myself
A half-done feature is never landed. Landing with a feature
flag off is an explicit option, only if it was designed that way
Raising the budget resumes parked tasks in priority order
Nothing starts over. A retired model uses the roster fallback

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Undo a merged feature is a current-feature change, not a blind reset
1 Inventory: commits, files, routes, exports, migrations, packages,
env, config, jobs, and external effects
2 Who else uses each piece: edges, imports, columns, later migrations
3 Classify. Only this feature: remove
Shared, including a feature mid-build: keep, and move ownership
Data: keep. Dropping is an explicit choice, export first,
and expand-then-contract
A package: remove only if nothing else imports it
An external effect cannot be undone. Show the receipts
A compensating action, such as unregistering a webhook, is a task if possible

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: How to execute the undo

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Revert that merge. Run the regression
Recorded as a forward revision, so it can itself be undone

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Removal tasks per area, verified like any other task,
then the regression of features that shared a boundary

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
On open, before anything runs, reconcile
Last revision, outbox, expired leases fenced
Missing worktrees recreated from checkpoints
New base commits, dirty files, branch switches, edits in worktrees
Lockfile and tool versions. Tokens, reset windows, prices, models
A CLI version change reruns the adapter conformance suite
Each open question is rechecked against the new commits and answers

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Welcome back. Finished while away. Parked, and why
Questions waiting, including one a commit may already answer
Your commits, and any overlap that will refresh a task
Connections. Budget left. Nothing runs until Resume
Review, or open the board, still starts nothing
Each question gets a recap: the decision, why it is needed,
and what the new commits changed. Older than a week: re-validate
Obsolete questions are retired with a note
Deleted checkpoint refs: those tasks restart from the brief
Finished work on integration stays. Abandoned export branches
remain theirs. The feature is marked abandoned

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Infer or ask, when a criterion is resolved, a worker or planner
meets a missing product decision, or a steer may change one
The kernel rejects a break of these rules. One object per criterion
Do not invent criteria. Propose a new gap separately, with its source

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Which status is actually earned?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
explicit. Cite the exact span
Your own earlier summary is not evidence

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
derived. Name the rule and the premises
No circular support. Never for a costly choice

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
delegated. Pick inside those limits
Record the reason. A recommendation alone is not this

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: missing, partial, or conflict

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Quote, do not paraphrase. The quote must establish the value
Negation and retraction win. Keep digits and negations as spoken
Paid services, identity, retention, deleting data, and legal duties
are explicit, or an explicit bounded delegation. Never derived
One criterion at a time. Two readings is a conflict. Do not pick one
In an existing repo, code is today. The request is the change

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Must a question be asked?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
One concrete question, in their words
The decision, why it matters, the options,
a recommendation when one is clearly safer, and something else
If two readings change behavior, show both

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Return id, status, value, evidence, rule, premises,
delegation, missing detail and question

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Before returning: a stranger would agree each explicit quote
establishes that value. Every derived value names a rule and
resolved premises. No costly choice is derived
Nothing is credited from a retracted or superseded span

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
SQLite is the source of truth. Markdown and Mermaid are views
An edit of a view is a proposal. It is never applied in place
Only the coordinator writes. Agents send typed requests
Coding stays parallel. Recording a result is the serialized part
Each record has a version. Each change set has a global revision
Freshness uses the read set, never the global number

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Who changed a view?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Watcher on .harness/views, debounced
A temp-file save counts as one edit

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Hash scan against the export manifest
at start, on open, and every 10 minutes

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Diff of views between two state-branch commits

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Parse sections by markers: record ID, version, hash
Unchanged hash: skip. Fields diff exactly. Prose diffs as text
Links and ef-fields compared with stored edges
Text outside a marker: doc-import proposes what it is. Shown, not applied
A broken marker: match by heading. Low confidence asks which record
A Mermaid edit: arrows between known nodes become relation proposals
Layout-only changes are ignored

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Review card. Nothing applies without Enter
Impact is shown. Apply both, or discard
One change set, origin markdown_edit. Then the same rules as chat

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Database still at the marker's version?

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Clean apply

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Field-level merge, shown

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Conflict card. You choose. No automatic prose merge
While pending, that file is not overwritten

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: File or section removed?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
No record is deleted. Restore is the default
Retire these items is explicit, with impact

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: A proposal to retire that record. Never automatic

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Recognized by ef_file. Content is imported
The view is regenerated at its standard path

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Pending edits affect no agent
An applied edit holds or refreshes only attempts whose read set contains it

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
One write connection. WAL so readers do not block
Workers have no database access. MCP and typed proposals only
UI and exporters read a committed revision
A second process is read-only: owner row, BEGIN IMMEDIATE, and a file lock
Option A and hybrid writers were rejected: enforcement would sit in foreign code

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Bookkeeping only. Model calls, Git and exports are outside the transaction
Group commit every few milliseconds. One savepoint per request
Heartbeats stay in memory. Token streams are not stored
Bounded queues. Telemetry yields to task transitions
Target: 50 simulated workers, p99 under 50 ms

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: What could go wrong?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: BEGIN IMMEDIATE. Retry the whole transaction

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: One conditional update. Success is exactly one row changed. Epoch increments

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Valid only if the epoch matches at commit
A submission that arrived in time is not expired for queue delay

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Operation ID, persisted before send. A repeat returns the stored receipt
Candidates are also unique by task, attempt and commit
No receipt means not recorded

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Roll back. Safe mode: stop dispatch, keep worktrees and checkpoints

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: data_version changed. Integrity check, then safe mode

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Record version and content hash. Edge-set version. History is immutable
Global revision labels snapshots and exports. It does not decide freshness
A change set stores origin, what it read, old and new versions, and a class
Cosmetic: non-normative prose. Clarifying: consistent detail, owner plus gate
Compatible: structured diff. Breaking: value, removal, or unmarked normative text

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Class, for each dependent

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Regenerate the view. Tasks are left alone

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Not started: refresh the brief
Running: a steer at the next boundary
Submitted: verify on current checks
Accepted: re-verify. A new receipt if it still passes

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Not started: refresh, and the planner reviews scope
Running: hold, refresh, resume or a fresh session
Submitted: verify on the new checks after the planner updates them
Accepted: re-verify. Rework only if a check fails, or new behavior has no task

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Walk reverse edges, breadth first, bounded
If a regenerated brief or check has the same hash, stop. Early cutoff
Acceptance compares the read set with current versions
A breaking difference cannot be accepted until current checks pass
Optimistic change sets recompute if their read versions moved
Disjoint sets both commit. Same record: the owner, or the developer if both are explicit
Five edits of one contract: one impact run

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Authentication, as specified
A-021 gains Google. Breaking. CS-88, revision 215
Planner publishes C-014 v2, task T-018, and updates the check only if needed
T-014 is re-verified and stays accepted. A running consumer gets a steer
New workers get v2. Unrelated tasks never notice

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Tests: 50 workers, no double holder, no lost receipt, no stale epoch
Crash before the receipt: retry writes exactly one row
Edit a view while closed, then change the same record: a conflict, nothing overwritten
Delete the views folder: records stay, files regenerate
An unrelated fact holds zero tasks. A compatible contract change only steers consumers

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5;

span.p: 7 · Safety: sandbox, network, supply chain

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5;

span.p: Sandbox, network policy and what text cannot grant · sandbox-and-security.mmd

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: A · MXC

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: B · Sandbox users

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: C · Restricted token

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: D · Container or WSL2

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: None acceptable

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Coding worker or its command

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Tests, verifier, dev server

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Kernel installer

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Researcher

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Vendor process, not its commands

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The boundary is the OS, not tool names. Every process an attempt starts runs sandboxed
Wrapped mode, the default: the whole vendor process tree runs in the sandbox
and keeps its native tools. Network: its provider and loopback MCP only
Logins: a client-supplied token or API key. Never a Claude subscription token
Stripped mode, the fallback: vendor shell off, harness.run over MCP,
file reads limited by its permission rules, subagents, hooks and web tools off
Our loop: harness.run and our edit tool. Codex: its own OS-enforced sandbox
Each harness.run gets its own Job Object. harness.start_service for servers
Wrapped agents have their own small cap. Everyone else shares a warm run pool
Conformance: .ssh unreadable by every native tool, non-provider web refused

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Strongest tier this PC can use

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Microsoft Execution Containers. No admin
Writes, secret reads and network enforced. Loopback allowed

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Two low-privilege users, once, with admin
ACLs plus firewall. Reads, writes and network enforced

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
No admin. Writes enforced. Secret reads are not
Network is advisory only. Yellow badge
Allowed only when the task needs no network and no untrusted code
Installs and dev servers need A, B or D
Foreign agents here: stripped mode only, Tier C tasks only

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Optional. Full enforcement, and Linux parity with CI

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Writable: this attempt's worktree, temp and build output
Read-only: toolchains, the package store, Git objects
Denied reads: .ssh, cloud creds, browser profiles, the vault area,
harness data, other worktrees, the developer's checkout
Only the kernel writes .git. Environment is scrubbed. HOME is inside the attempt
One Job Object: CPU, memory, process count, kill the tree
Wall-clock limits. A separate desktop where Windows supports it
A Job Object alone does not stop file or network access. The tier does

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Hold the task and explain. Never run unsandboxed in silence
An explicit project override shows a red banner on every card and receipt

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Who wants the network?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
No direct internet
harness.fetch_docs and harness.read_package_source only

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Loopback only, plus declared test hosts through an allowlisting proxy

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Package registries only, through the proxy

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: No direct internet. Doc fetcher, read-only, no side effects

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Its provider's API only

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Allowlisted docs and pinned READMEs. Strip scripts, hidden text
and invisible Unicode. Plain Markdown, size cap, cached by URL and hash
Returned as untrusted quoted material, with source and date
Prefer the installed package's own types and source
Workers do not browse: an injected page must not meet write access

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Workers never install. They send an intent. The integrator approves
The kernel installs with pnpm 10, whose scripts are blocked by default
A real build step is approved once and pinned. New packages are checked
for age, known vulnerabilities, typosquats and license
The lockfile is the only install source. npm and Yarn: scripts off,
then approved scripts run explicitly

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Text cannot grant power. Tools, paths, network and budget come from
the brief and the kernel. Context is labeled instruction, user, or data
Researchers read and cannot act. Workers act and do not browse
Every model output is schema-checked. Unknown actions are rejected
Diffs are scope-checked. Commands are allowlisted
harness.flag_blocked stops on a suspicious or contradictory instruction
The meta-lab plants injections and fake secrets and checks they are not followed

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Data folder is not readable by other users
Secrets stay in Credential Manager. Sandbox users cannot read DPAPI
Transcripts stay local. Raw audio is kept only if the developer turns it on
The redactor runs on logs, traces, diagnostics, exports and prompts
BitLocker is recommended. The database is not encrypted by the app in v1

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
What is protected: files outside the project, credentials, the checkout,
harness state and held-back tests, other attempts, accounts, and the plan
Who we assume: a confused model, injected text, a malicious package,
a malicious skill, or a worker editing tests

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A test that needs one host: the brief names it. The proxy allows that host
A network drive that cannot be ACL'd: tier A or D, or move the project
A missing tool: a human step or an approved toolchain install
A dev server binds loopback only, on a port for that attempt
Disabling the sandbox: red banner, recorded on every receipt

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5;

span.p: 6 · Building and verifying

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5;

span.p: Mystery bugs and repo-wide sweeps · investigations-and-sweeps.mmd

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: No. A symptom, unknown files

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Many files, one change

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Only a new guard, null check or try/catch

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Yes

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Yes, a normal task

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Code only. Recommended

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Code and database

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Code, database and public API

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Known write scope?

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Investigation. Read widely. Write almost nothing
1 Intake: symptom card. Ask the missing facts once
2 Reproduce: tests/repro only. Fail for the reported reason,
in a clean environment. Repeat to measure flakes
3 Localize: temporary logs on a quarantined branch
4 Prove: a second model checks the note. A minimal change
flips the test, and undoing it flips it back
5 Fix: a normal task, scope = the proven files
6 Keep: the reproduction joins the permanent suite
No reproduction, no fix. Each stage has a cap
Hypotheses are logged. The same experiment is refused
Past the cap: ask for a recording or HAR, or ship logging behind a flag

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A sweep changes a symbol, dependency or pattern across features,
or more than 15 files. It is the only owner of those paths
Exclusive lease on the compiler and search result
Maintenance window: drain in-flight work there, start no new work there,
leave unaffected work running
Branch harness/s/id from integration, landed like a feature
Afterwards, briefs are rewritten from the symbol map and re-checked

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Choose by evidence
Used to work, and a good commit exists: git bisect run
One engine only: differential run, compare network, cookies, console
Intermittent: many runs, jitter, traces of pass and fail
Server-side: correlation ID, temporary spans
Data-dependent: shrink the input to the smallest failing case

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Safari logout, as specified
WebKit: cookie missing after the checkout redirect
Chromium keeps it. SameSite=Strict is dropped on the way back
Lax flips the test. Revert flips it back
Fix scope is the session file. A reviewer checks the auth rules

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Does the fix touch the proven mechanism?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Flag it. Two tests must pass: the symptom, and the mechanism
Reverting the fix must fail both. reviewer asks: cause, or cover?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Reproduction stays. Full regression runs

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Ordinary leaf task. This document does not apply

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Rename of code, data, or a public API?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Types, files and functions. Tables and routes stay

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Plus expand-then-contract

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Old routes stay as aliases for a deprecation period

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
1 Read-only research: guide, changelog, known codemods
2 Official codemod, language-service rename, ts-morph, ast-grep
or jscodeshift. A model may write a script that is reviewed, then run
3 Checklist: type errors, tests, lint, and string hits
4 Residual fixes in dependency order. One commit per batch
5 Type check, full suite, journeys, leftover scan
6 Senior review of the non-mechanical diff
Cannot submit while an error, a failing test or an unallowlisted leftover remains
Parallel only when partitions are disjoint and each compiles alone

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
1 Symptom patches are flagged. Two regression tests
2 Bisect only a stable fingerprint. Exit 125 skips a broken commit
Fresh sandbox per step. Confirm by reverting on current code
3 Search every name form, including strings, SQL, config and docs
Persisted names are keep or migrate, never a silent rename
4 All-or-nothing leases. Intent mode. Tasks do not wait while holding
Overlapping sweeps are serialized
5 Packets fit the model. Hunks, not whole-file rewrites
Elision placeholders are refused
6 Behavior-preserving sweeps record characterization tests first
AST flags await, defaults, ?? versus or, equality and timeouts
7 Start from latest integration. Land in stages. Recompute the checklist
after merging. Schema changes take the schema lease
8 Workers never write the knowledge database. One test database per attempt
Retry from a fresh worktree and database. Sweeps resume from the last batch
9 Several projects share one broker, with an interactive lane
10 SQLite is inside the app. The CLI is optional and read-only
A foreign commit is seen via data_version, then integrity check and safe mode

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Cannot reproduce: stay open, with the hypothesis log
Cause is a dependency: upgrade, patch or workaround, with the upstream link
The report is a missing feature: send it to discovery
No compatible library version: stop, and offer pin, replace or wait
The developer edits during a sweep: merge, then recompute the checklist

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5;

span.p: Tokens, one kit, and point-to-fix · ui-design-system.mmd

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: A feature's screen
