span.p: Not in any task

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Web frontend pack. Every question has a recommended answer,
so Accept all works
A reference site: none, use a clean neutral
Brand: slate, with one indigo accent. Density: balanced
Theme: both, following the system. Font: the system stack
Kit: shadcn/ui on Tailwind, source copied into the repo
An existing repo extracts Tailwind, CSS variables and the
component folder, and shows them for confirmation instead of asking

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Phase 0, before any screen worker
tokens.json, W3C design tokens. Color roles, six type steps,
4 px spacing, radii, shadows, motion. Light and dark
CSS variables and the Tailwind theme are generated, not hand-edited

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
One kit. Button, Card, Input, Table, Dialog, Toast, page header
Each has variants and the states default, hover, focus,
disabled, loading and error
Templates: app shell, page header with an actions slot,
list/detail, form, empty, error

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
/__styleguide renders every primitive, variant, state
and template, in light and dark
Screenshots at desktop, tablet and phone are the reference crops
when the developer supplied none
Conventions are quoted into briefs: page header for titles,
primary actions in the header slot, Table rather than a custom grid

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A screen task gets a spec, not a picture
Route, template, regions, states, density, and which crops to match
The accessible names are also the test contract
A box-and-label wireframe can be approved in the plan preview
Workers compose the kit. They do not invent look-alikes
They may only use tokens

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
After the task
Block: raw colors, arbitrary pixels, new fonts, look-alike components
Block serious axe-core issues: labels, roles, contrast, focus
Block layout at three widths: no overflow, overlap or clipping,
tap targets at least 24 px
Warn: header height, page padding and spacing rhythm
Advise only: a Senior vision review against the crops
Pixel diff blocks only after the developer approves a baseline

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
App tab runs harness/integration, or a chosen feature branch,
in its own browser port and profile

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Point mode. Hover outlines. A click captures
route, role, accessible name, DOM path,
component and source file and line from the dev-only plugin,
a highlighted crop, computed spacing and type,
and the owning task from path ownership
The composer target becomes that element
A dragged box can point at a gap between elements

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: What was asked?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A visual change for that feature's owner
Example: KitchenCard padding down one spacing step

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A change to the screen spec
Example: Print moves into the page-header actions slot
Tests find it by role and name, so the journey still passes

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Who owns the file?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: That feature's owner. A normal change

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The design-system owner
Preview the affected screens before applying

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: The owning feature, as an override inside tokens

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: The project planner. Brownfield code outside the plan

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
When it finishes: before and after, side by side
Accepting updates the approved baseline
Anything still off is another message

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A screenshot mid-build becomes a crop for the screens it covers
The design owner checks tokens and previews the effect first
Two workers want the same new primitive: one is built, both use it
'Make this red' uses a token role or a named variant. Raw values stay blocked
If the preview will not start: show the error and the owning task,
and offer the last good build
No design system yet: extract what exists, offer to consolidate tokens,
never restyle the whole app unasked

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5;

span.p: Static audit and the traceability gate · completeness-gate.mmd

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Yes

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: No

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: No

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Yes

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
DRAFTED, READY, LEASED, CODING, then STATIC_AUDIT, then clean verify
A static failure returns to coding. It is not a verification attempt
The same fingerprint three times escalates like any loop

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Deterministic scans on the diff. Seconds. No tokens. Shown to the worker
TODO, FIXME, stubs, empty catch, dead controls, hard-coded records,
fake names outside fixtures, mock imports in product code
Edits to protected tests, skip or only, ts-ignore, as any, eslint-disable
Unreachable files, unused planned fields, missing contract surface
Elision placeholders, unplanned large deletions, out of scope, secrets
A real deferral is TODO of an approved ID, and it appears in the final report
Seeds, fixtures and declared generated paths are excluded
A language with weak AST still gets text and type scans, and says so

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Hard finding?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Reject with locations. Repeated identical failures escalate

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Soft findings stay on the receipt for high-risk review:
a tiny diff, complexity far below the rules, branches on visible examples

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The database holds requirements, tasks, checks, results and waivers
Graph compile refuses to publish unless:
every in-scope requirement has a task and a check
every task has a requirement
every rule-bearing requirement has a held-back or generated check
A waiver is low-risk, or the developer approved it
400 edge cases and 320 tasks: publish fails and lists the 80

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The implementing worker does not write the checks
Red before green: a new check must fail on the code before the task
A surviving mutation means the check is too weak
The final audit samples pairs. A Manager asks whether the check
observes the requirement. Disagreement goes to the planner

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Every linked check passed
for this artifact, including in-scope rules?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Rejected. Missing checks are listed
A feature stays open until every one of its requirements passes
at the current versions

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Accepted

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Tests are read-only. The verifier runs them
Held-back and generated cases make hard-coding fail
flag_blocked and dispute_test are the cheap honest exits
The worker prompt says: disagree, stop, never special-case
The hint ladder caps retries, because more feedback increases gaming
A Senior review of high-risk diffs is advisory
A detected shortcut lowers that model's pass-rate for the class

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
I fixed it myself runs the same audit
The developer may override a finding, and that override is recorded

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5;

span.p: Verifying screens, routes, migrations and AI features · verification-for-real-apps.mmd

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: A screen or route was checked

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: The entry point is an internal name

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: A migration

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: A model-powered feature

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: The named control or route is absent

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: It exists, and the result is wrong

span.p: Third

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: A screen or route was checked

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The planner publishes how the product is used, not how it is built
Visible to the worker: route, accessible names, landmarks,
empty, loading and error text, and a test id only where no
user-facing name exists
The worker is free on structure, CSS, files and markup
Hidden with the verifier: the seeded data and the expected results
Tests find things the way a person does. Role and name, not a CSS id
An ARIA snapshot checks the region. A refactor that keeps the
visible behavior keeps passing

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
How the verifier drives it
Screen: Playwright role and label locators, on the attempt
API: HTTP on the attempt's server. Path, method, schemas,
error codes. Schema validation, plus the expected values
Auth: routes, redirects, session properties, failure behavior.
A local mock identity provider covers valid login, bad state,
expired code and wrong role
Job: trigger and observable output, with a fake clock
CLI: command, flags, exit code and output format, in the sandbox
Time rules need an injectable clock. Fake timers at the boundary
instants, in the stated zone. Performance: repeated runs, a
tolerance, a stated dataset size. Concurrency: two clients,
assert the documented outcome

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: What has to be decided next?

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: What failed?

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
After submit, a separate binder sees the inputs and the code,
never the expected values, and writes a small adapter
The adapter may not import expectations or edit product files
The trusted runner compares its observations with the hidden expectations
The entry point is named in the contract before coding.
Red-before-green runs against generated contract stubs, and only
a behavioral failure counts as red. A compile error is a binding bug
If it cannot find an entry point, that is a binding defect
for the author. The brief was underspecified. Not a worker failure
A user-facing entry needs no binder. The runner uses the contract

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Migration, on a fixture at the previous schema
Synthetic edges: nulls, Unicode, max lengths, duplicates,
boundary dates, orphan-looking rows. Tier 3
Assert row counts, checksums of stable columns, each mapping rule,
constraints, indexes, and the app's read path
Run again: it is safe to repeat, or it refuses cleanly
A down-migration round-trips. A slow fixture may shrink,
if the smaller set still covers every rule, and that is recorded
Renames, type changes and drops use expand, then contract:
add new, copy, switch reads, remove old later

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Split the feature
Shell: exact tests with a stub model, including malformed output.
Prompt, parsing, schema, retries, fallbacks, cost limits
Properties: schema, required facts, length, no forbidden content
Quality: a planner eval set of 10 to 30 cases. A judge different
from the generator, a rubric, several samples, a stated threshold
Shown as a score, never a plain green tick
The developer can tighten or loosen the threshold
If the judge is down: verified except quality, and dependents
proceed only if the developer allows
Ordinary CI replays recorded responses. Deterministic, and free

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Contract mismatch. A plain message
It does not count as a hidden-check failure
The contract was already visible to the worker
Renaming Print to Print list is a product revision, not a worker fault
Two buttons with the same name are flagged at planning

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Behavior failure. The hidden-check rules apply
A wrong hidden API, auth, job or CLI result uses this same ladder

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Skip the ladder?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
No more retries at this level
Up one level with the full history, or back to the author
if the brief looks unclear

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Author review. The brief or the expectation is suspect

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: The author decides the dispute

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Which informed attempt is this?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Rule id and text, plus the failure type:
wrong value, missing, extra, wrong order, exception, timeout
The hidden input stays hidden

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A fresh example from the same rule, with expected and actual
The original held-back case stays hidden
A disclosed example joins the visible set. Another stays hidden
Each rule keeps at least three hidden examples
The ladder step lives in verification_state and survives attempts

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Visual layers, from blocking to advice
Structure: ARIA snapshot of landmarks and order. Blocks
Geometry: three widths, no overflow or overlap, within 2 px
of the template, minimum tap size. Blocks
Accessibility: axe-core. Serious issues block
Tokens: no raw colors or arbitrary spacing. Blocks
Pixels: toHaveScreenshot, dynamic regions masked.
Blocks only after an approved baseline
Taste: vision review against the style guide. Advisory

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
External services use that service's test mode or a local emulator
Record how it differs from live. A separately authorized live
check covers what remains
A flaky browser test reruns in a fresh state
A disagreeing run is unstable and goes to its owner

It is never truncated. About 2 to 3k tokens for a Junior, 4 to 6k for a Senior

span.p:
Convention lines for the files, library warnings,
signatures of accepted dependencies, tokens and kit pieces for UI

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Neighbor summaries, rationale, full research. Pull only

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A cross-cutting rule has a scope predicate, not a home document
The task declares routes, entities, screens, libraries and layers
Every rule is matched. A sign-up rule reaches an export that touches names
An architect's local rule that is really cross-cutting must be moved,
or marked local with a reason
Each in-scope rule names checks. Acceptance fails if those checks did not pass

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: The agent needs more

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
kb.search, kb.get, kb.neighbors, kb.contract, kb.why, kb.code
Full text first. Embeddings are optional
Call and token limits per attempt. Responses are data, not instructions
A miss becomes AskOwner. A real gap becomes a spec item
A revision pins the brief's version. Newest is opt-in

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: How was it obtained?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Declared dependency. If it changes: hold at the next boundary
and refresh the brief

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Observed dependency. At acceptance, recheck
A material change reruns verification on the new version

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Pulls are recorded by task class and whether the task passed
Weekly, the meta-lab may propose pushing a repeatedly pulled item
A predicate that lands in most packets, with no related failures,
is flagged so the architect can narrow it
A diff that touches more than the plan declared adds those facts,
and their checks, before acceptance

Can one worker implement and verify this

Decision versions, contracts, owned paths, state needs,

Catalog of about 20 skills, downloaded from the most-used public skills
and vetted. infer-or-ask is ours. Name, trigger, stack, digest

div.style: color: rgb(20, 58, 48) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

Pin skill IDs and digests

Ready to run?
Check references, skills, tool scope, context and reserved budget

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

Load required guidance once

Return failing rule and observation

span.p: Preset, cap, or level

span.p: Merge, split, reorder, defer

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Why, or can it be cheaper

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Planning starts on its own when discovery is ready
Show the token and dollar or plan-share estimate first
If planning itself would pass the budget, ask first
and offer a cheaper planner level

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
1 System architecture. system-architect, Manager
Components, skeleton data model, inter-feature contracts,
cross-cutting rules with scopes, name prefixes, conventions,
pinned versions, environment manifest
Code checks that every requirement maps, every contract has
a producer and a consumer, and names are unique

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
2 Master plan. master-planner, Manager
Phase 0: everything two or more features consume, plus conventions
Wave order, estimates, paperwork budget per wave
Each shared artifact has exactly one Phase 0 owner

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
3 Feature architecture and planning, just in time per wave
feature-architect and feature-planner, Seniors, in parallel
Flows, screen specs, tasks, visible examples, check slots, one wiring task
3b oracle-author writes the held-back cases, sealed, without the task split

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
4 Graph compile. Kernel
One DAG. No cycles. No two owners of a path or a name. Within size limits
Every requirement has a task and a check. Dependencies are edges

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
5 Estimates. Kernel. Tokens, money or allowance, and time, with ranges
Calibrated history when this developer has it

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
6 Crew proposal. Kernel. Three presets
Each must fit the budget, the connection caps and the machine

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Finished stages stream onto the canvas and can be opened
Cancel is available. A gap reopens only its own criterion

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Phase 0 is a walking skeleton plus the shared contracts
Thinking is done in synthesis, so the tasks are recipes
P0.1 Scaffold runs alone. Junior, low
Then, in parallel where write scopes do not overlap:
P0.2 Packages, one pinned lockfile change. Junior, low
P0.3 Skeleton schema, migration 0001, seed recipe. Mid, or Junior if simple
Feature-only columns arrive later as additive migrations
P0.4 Shared types and validators. Junior, low
P0.5 Auth skeleton, only if two features need it. Mid
P0.6 Test harness and a passing smoke test. Junior, low
P0.7 Tokens, primitives, shell, style guide. Mid
P0.8 .env.example, manifest, CI if requested. Junior, low
Generators make the scaffold mechanical once the decisions exist
An existing repo shrinks Phase 0 to the safety net, the baseline,
shared migrations or types, and extracted conventions

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Foundation gate on harness/integration
Build, lint, smoke test, migration on an empty database,
style guide page renders

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Conventions are quoted into each brief
Lint makes them executable: no new packages outside intents,
no redefining a shared type, no raw colors outside tokens
Shared files belong to the integrator. Workers send an intent

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Feature waves wait. The check goes to the Phase 0 owner
Repeated failure escalates to the Manager

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Level per task, from the planner, checked by code
Rules, contracts, write-scope size, held-back cases,
similar tasks, risk tier
Mechanical is Junior. Standard is Mid
Tricky is Senior. Integration or architecture is Manager
The developer is the CEO

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Critical risk, a very large context,
or a past failure on a similar task?

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Bump one level

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Compare expected cost, not the sticker price
Cost per attempt, divided by the chance of passing
A cheap model that often fails can be the expensive one
Start from defaults. Calibrate on this developer's history
Roster maps level to connection, model and effort
It is versioned, because model names change. The sample roster is illustrative

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Workers this wave = the minimum of
ready tasks at once, measured machine slots,
each connection's concurrency cap, the developer's maximum,
and what the budget pace allows
Then critical-path list scheduling: the ready task with the
longest chain behind it, on the best free slot
More workers than the graph's width do not help
Integration cost is why width is also capped
Thinking width and execution width are separate: commands share
a warm pool of 2 to 4 sandboxes. Wrapped agents have a lower cap

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Preset

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Widest. Raise the level of critical-path tasks
Kitchen illustration: 7 peak, about 38 min

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Cheapest level that still meets the pass-rate target
Width limited by pacing. Illustration: 5 peak, about 55 min

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Lowest viable levels. Narrower, to stay inside plan windows
Illustration: 3 peak, about 1 hour 40 min

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Preview: Phase 0, feature waves, crew, time range,
dollar or allowance range, and tasks that rest only
on choices made for you. Peak count changes by wave
A single chain is one worker plus the Manager, and the preview says why
A small machine limits stateful tasks. A low connection cap
limits width, and is named as the reason

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Developer

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The first build of a project always waits for this
Revisions may auto-start: at most 5 tasks, 1 dollar, 2 percent
of a plan window, and no must-ask, breaking contract, destructive
migration, new dependency or external effect. Daily cap 5 dollars
or 10 percent. Otherwise they show a preview

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A request to the owning planner
The preview updates when they republish

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
While building: the hint ladder, then up one level or back to the author
Reschedule when tasks finish early or late
A free worker takes the next ready task
Record class, level, model, tokens, time and pass or fail
A roster change applies to new attempts only

span.p: Build · one wave at a time

span.p: Upfront · before Phase 0

Size is computed from the entities, roles, screens, endpoints and rules
A line count is an output, never a target

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Generators are code. Most cells cost no tokens
They emit only what exists
Permission: entity, action, role. Fields: type, limits, who sets them
Lifecycle: states, transitions, who, side effects
Screen states. Every control: action, disabled, feedback
Endpoint failures. Boundaries: before, at, after. Zero, one, many, max
Concurrency of two actors. Lists: sort, page, search, empty, huge
Deletion and retention. Notifications. Formatting of dates and money
Thousands of identical cells collapse to one scoped rule

source decisions, risk, and an oracle sketch
Ubiquitous: the system shall. Event: when. State: while
Unwanted: if, then. Optional: where the feature is included
The planner later turns the oracle into a check

span.p:

no unresolved contradiction, no critical question open
The screen counts explicit, derived, defaulted, proposed and asked
Proposed items can be accepted, edited or rejected
Generators and layers 1 to 4 are free. The expander is Mid, per feature,
only for cells that need judgement. This spends the paperwork budget

span.p:
Chat on the left. Canvas on the right. Divider drags
The canvas can pop out. Tabs: Architecture, Plan, Tasks, App, Diff
Every box is a real node with a stable id. No second diagram state
React Flow, ELK layout. Dragged positions are kept
Mermaid export is the shareable text view
The canvas is not generated from Mermaid

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Mic fills an editable draft. Nothing is sent until Send
Local Whisper by default. OS recognizer as fallback. Zero tokens
Web Speech is not the default: Chrome sends audio to Google,
and it is unreliable in Electron. Cloud transcription is not the default
A ChatGPT plan token does not cover the transcription API
Grey while a phrase is unstable, black when it is final
3 seconds: still listening. 60 seconds: mic off, draft saved
Numbers, times, money, names and negations: amber if unsure,
with alternatives on hover. 'Scratch that' stays as spoken
Optional one-click strike-through. The resolver, after Send,
reads the whole message, including the retraction

span.p:
One resolve of the whole message
Canvas: Reading your message, then highlight the diff
No model graph while speaking
Echo times, amounts, counts and names in bold

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Readiness in words, never a lone percentage
Needed before building. Everything we know
Say why the total rose or fell, and link those items
Hover lists them. Items that can wait say so

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Composer target. Exactly one

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Enter answers that card
Recommended option is highlighted, never auto-sent
Nothing is accepted on a timer

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: A message about that box. It does not answer a question

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: A visual change for the pointed-at element

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Normal chat routing

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Selection never answers. The question card stays, dimmed,
its option kept, labeled Paused. Each target has its own draft
Focus is captured when typing starts. A new question waits below
After a box message, return to the focused question, with a toast
Lasso or Ctrl+click: the target reads N boxes, one clause each

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Does the text fit this target's type?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Ask once: answer the paused question, or keep it on this box

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: What kind of box message?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Read-only. Source quote and basis. No state change

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Replace the interpretation. History: corrected transcription
Dependents update as for any other change

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: A new user fact supersedes the old one

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: A new linked rule. It may open a question

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Show what loses its prerequisite

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Read-only traversal. No tokens
Still works if the model allowance is used up
A real change then waits as a draft

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Correct, or a new decision?
And it is ambiguous

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Preset: I said this, it was misheard

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Preset: I changed my mind
The downstream effect is the same. The history label differs

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Impact preview before anything is applied. No tokens
Which tasks pause, which are not started, which keep running
Apply or Cancel. Apply is a normal revision

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Project stage

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Update the decision and the readiness counts

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Replan the affected tasks. The estimate updates

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Hard or soft holds. Unaffected work continues

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: A forward revision, with change or removal tasks

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A box can be an actor, feature, workflow step, rule, field,
contract, external service, screen, open question, assumption,
deferred item, today module, task, or edge
The popover shows that type's facts and its quick actions
An open question becomes the focused card
Today describes current code and is not edited in place:
'change this' becomes a planned change linked to that module
A running task is a message to its owner, not to the worker
Per-box history is in the popover and in the main chat

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The box changed while you typed: show both values, then ask
The box was deleted: fall back to General, keep the draft
Two boxes, 'make these the same': ask which value wins
The message names a different box: the exact name wins, and is echoed
Ctrl+Z before Enter is text undo. After apply, it is a forward revision
200 or more nodes: collapse by feature, zoom from system
to features to rules to tasks, plus search and filters

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Stage comes from opening question 4, what the demo must prove,
and question 5, the constraints. Chip: Prototype, MVP, Production
The developer can change it. Changing it later reopens only the
criteria whose applicability changed, and says how many
Running tasks continue unless a new decision affects their contract
One catalog, and the stage decides what applies,
the same idea as OWASP ASVS levels. The chip is the appetite
Options carry consequences, in the ADR sense

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Stage. Honesty stays.
The recommendation changes

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Scale, compliance, observability and multi-region
collapse to one line: not in this release
Simple local choices are recommended

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Basic privacy, errors, accessibility and deployment apply
Pragmatic defaults

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The full cross-cutting packs apply
Recommendations favor durability and auditability

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A risk trigger overrides the stage
Payments on a prototype still ask the payments questions

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Before a question is shown, code scores it
ask value = impact times uncertainty
impact = risk weight times dependents, plus one
uncertainty is 0 if evidence settles it, low if one option
dominates, high if the options really differ
Next questions are greedy maximum coverage, then this filter

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Must-ask, and not already
answered with evidence?

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Always ask, explicitly
Purpose and audience. Spending money. Real personal data
Identity and login provider. Hard to reverse. Legal or compliance
Or it contradicts what the developer already said
Autopilot never delegates one of these

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: How is this batch running?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Resolve with the recommendation
List it under Chosen for you. Never drop it silently

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Still shown, at the end of the batch, preselected
Accept all clears them

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Show it in the batch

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Soft cap per feature: about 10 on a Prototype,
about 25 in Production. Past the cap, remaining low-tier
questions go to Chosen for you. They are not dropped

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Every batch: recommended option preselected
An item already settled from evidence is shown, and needs nothing

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: dd_CREDIT

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: What the developer does

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Accepts every highlighted option in this batch
except must-ask, which stays for an explicit choice
Any of them can be changed first. Basis: explicit. Full credit

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Batch after batch until the architecture is complete
Stops only for must-ask, and says where it stopped
Opening five are must-ask, so Autopilot starts after them
Basis: delegated, with the risk bound and the stage
Full credit, and listed in Chosen for you

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: That answer is explicit. The rest of the batch stays

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Chosen for you stays visible. Any item reopens from the canvas
The plan preview flags tasks whose decisions were all delegated
A later explicit answer wins, and dependents are rechecked
'I never chose this' opens from the list, with batch and time
No matching recommend rule: the question is shown, not guessed
Two readings stay a conflict until the developer picks

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Versioned YAML, shared or project. On load: unique ids,
real criteria, acyclic prerequisites, real options,
must_ask only on high or critical. Never change an id's meaning
Lifecycle: draft, evaluated, active, deprecated
Active only after it changed a build on held-out projects
Promotion into the shared catalog is a reviewed edit, never automatic
Packs are the union of what opening review activates. Criteria deduped
Core, web, API, data and auth are deep. Payments are probe plus must-ask
Extension, mobile, desktop, CLI, AI and email are probe
Cross-cutting packs depend on the stage. About 200 in v1
A seam between two packs asks its questions once, not once per pack
Later: cloud, real-time, games, data pipelines

Show total detail and planning readiness separately
Include inherited criteria and display critical open count

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Five prompts about product, audience, workflow, demo and constraints
All together with folded examples or one at a time with examples open

Typing, dictation and optional graph preview
Keep focused card and answer options pinned while composing

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Explicit submit only
Reconcile the whole turn, withdrawals and corrections

span.p:
Opening reviewer checks five rubrics
Extract grounded claims and propose relevant domains

div.style: color: rgb(21, 61, 50) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Versioned decisions and evidence
User turn, quote, source revision, rule and premise IDs

div.style: color: rgb(21, 61, 50) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Freeze scoped criteria and fact versions for this round
Include project prerequisites and shared domains

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Union and deduplicate eligible questions
Filter settled, deferred, already-open and out-of-scope items

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Catalog indexes by domain and criterion
Generic rubrics, prerequisites, risk and allowed rules

div.style: color: rgb(68, 43, 12) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Score each question by uncovered criterion IDs
Break ties by blocking criteria, then stable ID

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Positive gain and room in batch?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Take the winner and remove overlap from temporary set
Keep persistent criteria open until answered

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Prepare selected questions and evidence only
Up to five, or two to three for a small change

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
For a catalog gap adapt a nearby rubric or create one local question
Link to an evidenced criterion, deduplicate and apply round budget

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Small resolver proposes explicit, derived, partial, missing, conflict or delegation
Each criterion gets its own evidence and value

div.style: color: rgb(68, 43, 12) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Kernel checks schema, current source spans and permitted rules
Reject retractions, invalid proof chains and cycles

div.style: color: rgb(68, 43, 12) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Independent meaning check on every derivation and costly explicit value
Difficult choices require a stated value or a bounded delegated choice

div.style: color: rgb(68, 43, 12) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Queue one focused question for missing detail
Options, free text, recommendation or explanation

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Bind reply to question and scope revision
Keep siblings, reconcile obsolete cards and new steers

div.style: color: rgb(21, 61, 50) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Commit supported criteria and new evidence
Credit each once. A delegated but unchosen value stays open.

div.style: color: rgb(68, 43, 12) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Nonempty current scope fully ready?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Explicitly deferred independent choice
Show milestone and block its consuming tasks until resolved

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Open known gaps in next round
Cap repeated generation and ask the highest-impact unresolved question

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Construct architecture and acceptance examples
Check cross-domain contracts, boundary cases and missing relations

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Activate validated architecture, plan, task and test revision
Show the plan preview. The first build waits for Start build

display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Git is required, and bundled as MinGit, so nothing is installed
Parallel work, checkpoints, undo, export as branches and
crash recovery are Git features. Plain copies, Jujutsu and
per-file editor snapshots do not replace them in v1
Mercurial or Perforce: not supported. Offer Work on a copy

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Developer picks a folder. The checkout is their desk
The harness never edits, stashes, resets or commits there
without an explicit click

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: What is in the folder?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Silent git init, branch main
The Phase 0 commit is scanned before it is made

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Set up Git, or work on a copy?
There is no continue-without-Git

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Before any baseline or snapshot: scan .env files, private keys,
high-entropy tokens, files over 50 MB, node_modules, build
output and OS junk. Show the .gitignore proposal and the
secrets that will not be committed. Accept, edit or cancel

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Copy into a new folder and set up Git there

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Record HEAD and the branch as the project base

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: You have uncommitted files

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Warn that landing may later need those files committed

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Wait, then recheck

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: No commits yet. The baseline is shown before it is made

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Merge, rebase, cherry-pick or conflicts: block.
Open in my editor. Never finish or abort it
Detached HEAD: pick a branch, or create harness-base and the date
OneDrive, Dropbox or a network folder: warn, continue or move
No user.name or email: one prompt, globals prefilled
Git missing from PATH: the bundled Git is used

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: What is being recorded?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Show what the baseline commit includes, then make it

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Dirty work is snapshotted, never moved. Stash is not used
Temporary index: GIT_INDEX_FILE, read-tree HEAD, add -A,
write-tree, commit-tree with parent HEAD,
store refs/harness/snapshots, then drop the temp index
Working tree, real index and branch stay untouched
The scan runs on the snapshot diff first. That commit is the workers' base
A later identical developer commit merges cleanly

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Developer's branch: landing target, only by a visible landing
harness/integration: accepted, tested work
harness/f/feature: private while its tasks land
harness/t/task/attempt: one leased attempt
refs/harness/checkpoints: WIP, kept for resume and export
Author is the role and agent id. Committer is the developer
Trailers: Harness-Task, Harness-Attempt
A human fix keeps the human as author

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Worktree outside the project, under LOCALAPPDATA
git worktree add --detach, then the attempt branch
core.longpaths. Registered on the attempt lease
Ignored files are absent, so the environment manifest supplies them
Secrets: env from the vault, never files
Local config: an allowlist copy. Dependencies: the lockfile,
with a shared package cache. Submodules init. LFS only for
the task's paths. Sparse checkout when the brief declares it
After retention: remove the worktree and prune
Checkpoint refs survive until the feature lands or the user deletes them

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Windows: short worktree root. Optional Defender exclusion
Keep .gitattributes, or the developer's autocrlf
Workers never rewrite line endings
Flag two paths that differ only by case
Stop the attempt's Job Object before deleting a locked tree
Predict a landing with git merge-tree --write-tree, before touching anything

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Existing repo, or a new one?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Folder is ready. Discovery uses the opening prompts

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Opening card from a local scan. Zero tokens spent
What would you like to change?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Read cheaply, ask the model last
L0, free: tree, languages, manifests, scripts, tests, CI,
docs, schema, migrations, .env.example names, Git churn
L1, free and local: tree-sitter symbols, reference graph,
entry points from routes, main and bin
L2, bounded and cached by blob hash: one module card
per area this request touches. Show the estimate first
L3, per task: exact files or spans at the pinned commit
The message chooses the L2 modules. The rest stay at L0 or L1
L0 and L1 never leave the machine. Mask secrets before L2
A local-only project uses a local model, or skips L2

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Five change prompts, prefilled from the scan and the message
What changes. Which part, and who uses it. One done example
What must not change. How you check it today
A mixed message splits. Separate readiness, shared project facts
Slow is not testable. Ask the page, today's number, and the target
Recommended default: p95 under 300 ms on a realistic dataset
Trace the route to the query. Seeded data or a sanitized dump
Record EXPLAIN ANALYZE or a timing harness
Acceptance: a Tier 3 benchmark, plus that page's existing tests

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Confirmation card, not a lecture. Source and confidence on each claim
Tick, correct or ignore. Confirmed claims become observed facts
A correction overrides the observation and links to it
Unreviewed claims stay observed, unconfirmed
High-confidence ones may be used. A medium one used by a task
is listed in that task's assumptions
Stale docs: code wins for today. Never rewrite the README
unless a task includes it. Conventions node is quoted into briefs
Canvas: Today in grey, Change in color, edges show what is touched

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Run install, build and tests
in an isolated copy?

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Baseline receipt

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Not measured. Every later acceptance still runs
a pre-change baseline for the checks it touches

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Targeted checks pass, and no new failures anywhere

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Known failing, by name. No new failures
Optional task to fix those. Workers are not blamed for them

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Unstable. Out of pass or fail until the owner stabilizes them

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Safety net first. A test runner only with approval
Characterization tests for the touched modules,
passing before and after

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Stop. Offer Make the build pass. Feature work waits

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Deleted worktree: fence it, recreate from the last checkpoint
gc or prune: refs survive, missing worktrees are recreated
Repo moved: relocate, then git worktree repair
Huge repo: measure, then lower parallelism or use sparse checkout
Shallow clone: worktrees work. Skip blame hotspots
Monorepo: ask which packages, and scan those deeply
Generated or vendored: out of maps and write scopes
Unsupported language: L0 stays, L1 is text search,
L2 uses the files the request names
A request that contradicts the schema is a planned change
New commits during discovery: pin the start commit,
refresh changed cards before planning

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5;

span.p: Desktop shell, daemon, installer and updates · desktop-app.mmd

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Idle

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Building

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Pause and quit

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Keep building

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Cancel

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: The app

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: The database

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Parked work

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Provider policy

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: A foreign CLI

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Windows first. The window is a viewer. harnessd owns the build
A utility process would die with the Electron shell, so the daemon
is detached and runs the Electron binary as plain Node
A named pipe for the current user, plus a session token:
no localhost port, so a web page cannot reach it
Not a Windows Service: Git config, the vault and plan logins
belong to the user. One daemon per Windows user

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Window: chat, canvas, cockpit, office. A crash reopens and reconnects
Electron main: tray, notifications, updates. The daemon keeps running
harnessd: coordinator per project, state.db, global broker,
adapters, MCP, sandbox launcher, MinGit, verifier, doc fetcher
Workers and verifiers: one attempt each. A crash returns to the checkpoint

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Close the window?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: The app quits. The daemon stops after a short grace period

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Hide to the tray. First time: still building, N workers
Tray: Open, Pause all, status, Quit

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Quit while building?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Checkpoint everything, about 10 seconds, then quit

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Sleep: pause dispatch, reconcile on wake. In-flight calls are unknown
Shutdown or sign-out: checkpoint inside the shutdown window
Anything missed resumes from the previous turn boundary
Prevent sleep while building is off by default
Start at sign-in is optional, for resumes after a plan window resets
A second launch focuses the existing window

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Installer, about 200 MB: Electron, daemon, UI, MinGit,
gitleaks, tree-sitter grammars, office art
On demand, size shown, SHA-256 from a signed manifest:
Whisper at first mic use. Playwright browsers at first browser tests
Node, pnpm or Python if the project needs them and they are missing
Ollama, LM Studio, Docker and WSL2 are never bundled
A bad checksum is refused. Downloads resume. Any component can be removed

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: What is updating?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Signed differential download in the background
Restart to update only after every task is parked
A live build says: applies after this build, or when you choose

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
user_version on each SQLite file
1 Park work, exclusive lock, VACUUM INTO a backup
2 Forward-only migrations. Additive directly; constraint changes
use SQLite's 12-step rebuild, then search indexes rebuild
3 quick_check and invariants. On failure, restore the backup
global.db first. Each project migrates on open; a failure marks
only that project needs repair. Hourly and daily backups too
Corruption: salvage, or restore, then replay harness-state and Git
An older app cannot open a newer database. It offers the backup

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Resume with the prompt and skill versions the task started with
New versions apply to the next attempt
Old checkpoint formats are upcast on read, never rewritten in place

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Signed JSON, checked daily. New dispatches use the new file
Only a revoked route parks running work, at the next boundary

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Its own installer. A new version runs the conformance suite
before that runtime gets new tasks

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Electron, React, TypeScript, React Flow, ELK, PixiJS
Daemon on the bundled Node. SQLite via node:sqlite, FTS5,
better-sqlite3 only as fallback. Git is MinGit, not a library
ACP, MCP and vendor SDKs. Playwright. NSIS via electron-builder, signed
Electron and Node versions move together, checked in CI

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Logs, traces and crash dumps stay on this PC. Nothing is sent
JSON logs for 14 days, secrets redacted before they are written
A span per transaction, attempt, model call, tool, Git op and verification
Health page: queues, rate limits, latency, verifier time, sandbox denials
Help, Export diagnostics: a redacted bundle, previewed before it is saved

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Two Windows users: separate daemon, pipe, data and sandbox identities
Daemon still on the old version: park, exit, start the new one
Disk: warn at 15 GB, no new dispatch at 5 GB, Pause all at 2 GB
Antivirus quarantine: name the file, re-download and verify
Moving the data folder: park, move, repair worktree paths
